For those unaware, Cracked was purchased from Demand Media by E.W. Scripps for $39 mil last year at a time when E.W. Scripps was making a net yearly income of 28 million. E.W. Scripps has done very poorly since.

Last month they released their third-quarter results for this year:

For the quarter, the net loss was $26.7 million or 32 cents per share. In the prior-year quarter, net income was $12.5 million or 15 cents per share. The current-year quarter included a non-cash goodwill and intangibles impairment charge for Cracked of $35.7 million as well as $2.4 million of restructuring charges, which increased the net loss by $24 million (net of taxes) or 29 cents per share.

Goodwill impairment reflects the loss (or perceived loss) in value of a company after it's been purchased, basically meaning E.W. Scripps bought Cracked for $39 million and then, a year later, decided they had overpaid by $35.7 million.

So if you all were wondering why, after a solid decade of putting in inhuman hours and sacrificing their personal lives for the sake of building up this site, Jack O'Brien and Soren seemingly randomly jumped ship within 3 months of each other, well, this may be worth considering.

Besides them, this move makes a few other things more clear, like the sudden switch to asking for handouts/a subscription model to see more content from your favorite Cracked personalities. They never planned on delivering that extra content to you - they think Cracked’s worth 91% less than they paid (basically nothing), there was no way they were going to suddenly make that viable, and they knew it. This was about cashing in on every last drop of the good relationship Cracked’s talented cast worked tirelessly to build before canning them. The folks at E.W. Scripps knew they couldn’t afford to keep such talented faces, but also knew these folks were talented enough to have built an incredibly dedicated and engaged fanbase relationship. So E.W. Scripps cashed in on that relationship and, once there was no more to gain, got rid of the faces.

There’s a lot to be mad about here. For one, the sudden unemployment of some of the funniest, most talented, hard-working writers in the business. They truly don’t deserve this.

Two, the evaporation of one of the most significant collections of comedy talent out there. This website truly is greater than the sum of its parts. Sure, all the folks that were let go are too talented to go hungry, they’ll be fine, but they’ll likely never all work in the same building again, and that’s a tragedy. We’ve seen a few culturally huge online publications evaporate overnight in the past year or so, but this is by far the most heinous. It can’t be overstated how influential, how culturally important this website has been. To see this team unceremoniously disbanded… it’s numbing.

Three, E.W. Scripps callously taking advantage of the goodwill Cracked’s team earned from its fans from years of awesome, insomnia-inducing, social-life-crippling work. This site was built from basically nothing on the backs of these talented writers in exchange for years of their lives. E.W. Scripps wasn’t around for any of that – instead, they perform a buyout, immediately mismanage their new asset and, rather than understand what they have, opt to cash out and cut their losses. While we were out going to bars, hanging with friends, traveling, whatever, these writers were putting their personal lives on hold to pull all-nighters and deliver us an awesome quantity of hilarious, insightful content. They were building this site, and in a day, E.W. Scripps scrapped it for change.
